question: What is the main goal of the discussion chapter in a research project?

options.A: To explain what the results mean and why they matter
options.B: To list every raw statistical number generated by the data
options.C: To introduce brand new research questions not tested earlier
options.D: To summarize the literature review written in chapter two

explanation: The discussion moves beyond raw data to interpret meaning and clinical significance for readers. [learn more](BMP314_U3_T2#BMP314_U3_T2_h1)

question: Why is simply repeating statistics in the discussion chapter considered poor practice?

options.A: Because numbers belong exclusively in the literature review chapter
options.B: Because statistics do not explain the clinical meaning behind the data
options.C: Because examiners prefer qualitative descriptions over numerical data
options.D: Because raw data must be kept completely hidden until the oral defense

explanation: Examiners want to see interpretation and clinical insight, not just a carbon copy of the results section. [learn more](BMP314_U3_T2#BMP314_U3_T2_h1)

question: What should you do first before comparing your research results to published literature?

options.A: Select and prioritize the most important primary findings
options.B: Change the research questions to match the discovered data
options.C: Publish the preliminary draft in a local nursing journal
options.D: Delete all tables that contain non-significant p-values

explanation: Prioritizing key findings helps keep the discussion focused on the main objectives of the study. [learn more](BMP314_U3_T2#BMP314_U3_T2_h2)

question: If you have twelve different tables in your results, what is the best approach when starting your discussion?

options.A: Combine all twelve tables into one massive chart before writing
options.B: Ignore all numerical results and focus entirely on personal opinions
options.C: Discuss every single table in exact chronological order line by line
options.D: Focus the core narrative around the major clinically relevant findings

explanation: Attempting to give equal weight to minor details dilutes the main message of the research. [learn more](BMP314_U3_T2#BMP314_U3_T2_h2)

question: Why must a researcher connect their study findings to previously published literature?

options.A: To show how the current work fits into the wider scientific context
options.B: To increase the total word count of the thesis document
options.C: To prove that previous researchers made mistakes in their calculations
options.D: To avoid having to collect original data from pregnant women

explanation: Relating new data to past studies validates the research and demonstrates academic thoroughness. [learn more](BMP314_U3_T2#BMP314_U3_T2_h3)

question: Which type of study is most useful to include when comparing your own midwifery research findings?

options.A: Outdated textbooks published more than fifty years ago
options.B: Opinion pieces written by authors with no clinical background
options.C: Studies using similar populations, variables, or methodologies
options.D: Studies investigating completely unrelated medical conditions

explanation: Apples-to-apples comparisons provide the most meaningful context for evaluating new research outcomes. [learn more](BMP314_U3_T2#BMP314_U3_T2_h3)

question: What does concordance mean when comparing research results with published literature?

options.A: A complete mathematical error in the statistical analysis
options.B: The total rejection of the null hypothesis by the researcher
options.C: Agreement or harmony between your findings and past studies
options.D: An unresolvable disagreement between two external authors

explanation: Concordance indicates that your results mirror what others have previously discovered. [learn more](BMP314_U3_T2#BMP314_U3_T2_h4)

question: What is the best way to handle a finding that completely contradicts major published studies?

options.A: Pretend the unexpected finding never appeared in the data tables
options.B: Immediately fail the research project for producing incorrect data
options.C: Blame the participants for giving dishonest answers during interviews
options.D: Explore possible reasons like sample differences or changing clinical practice

explanation: Discrepancies are valuable learning points that often point to shifting trends or contextual differences. [learn more](BMP314_U3_T2#BMP314_U3_T2_h4)

question: When should you bring your theoretical framework back into the discussion chapter?

options.A: To interpret how the real-world data aligns with theoretical concepts
options.B: Never, because theory and practical data have no connection
options.C: Only when writing the literature review chapter for the first time
options.D: During the preliminary budget planning phase before data collection

explanation: The discussion chapter evaluates whether the chosen framework holds true against actual field data. [learn more](BMP314_U3_T2#BMP314_U3_T2_h5)

question: If your data shows pregnant women rejecting antenatal care due to a barrier in your theoretical model, how should you write this?

options.A: Claim that the statistical software made a calculation error
options.B: Remove the theoretical model from chapter two to avoid confusion
options.C: Explain how the data confirms the predictive power of the model's barrier construct
options.D: State that the theoretical model has been proven entirely useless

explanation: Connecting data back to the framework shows that the theory successfully explains real-world behavior. [learn more](BMP314_U3_T2#BMP314_U3_T2_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT an appropriate way to handle unexpected or unusual research findings?

options.A: Fabricating new data numbers to fit the original hypothesis
options.B: Exploring alternative clinical explanations for the anomaly
options.C: Discussing potential variables that may have skewed results
options.D: Acknowledging study limitations openly in the discussion text

explanation: Fabricating data is scientific misconduct; unexpected results should be analyzed and explained honestly instead. [learn more](BMP314_U3_T2#BMP314_U3_T2_h6)

question: Why can unexpected results actually strengthen a research thesis when handled properly?

options.A: They prove the researcher spent no time analyzing the data
options.B: They eliminate the need to write a conclusion chapter
options.C: They automatically guarantee international journal publication
options.D: They demonstrate critical thinking and thorough intellectual honesty

explanation: Examiners respect students who can critically evaluate anomalies rather than trying to sweep them under the rug. [learn more](BMP314_U3_T2#BMP314_U3_T2_h6)

question: What is the primary focus of the implications section in a Nigerian midwifery research project?

options.A: Proposing changes to international space travel policies
options.B: Listing the financial costs incurred during data collection
options.C: Translating study findings into practical actions for clinical care and policy
options.D: Complaining about the lack of government funding for higher education

explanation: Implications bridge the gap between academic theory and real-world improvements in healthcare delivery. [learn more](BMP314_U3_T2#BMP314_U3_T2_h7)

question: If your research shows poor maternity care increases home births, what is a fitting policy implication to write?

options.A: Concluding that midwifery education has zero impact on community health
options.B: Urging hospital management to conduct attitude-reorientation workshops for maternity staff
options.C: Suggesting that all rural health clinics be permanently closed down immediately
options.D: Demanding that pregnant women stop making decisions about their own bodies

explanation: Practical policy recommendations directly target the specific root problems identified by the research data. [learn more](BMP314_U3_T2#BMP314_U3_T2_h7)
